Correct ascertainment bias in the within-host SFS

Source: R/sfs.R
correctSFSBias.Rd

Deep sequencing imposes a detection threshold (e.g., 3%): sites with true frequency below this threshold are unobservable. This inflates the apparent fraction of moderate-frequency variants relative to rare variants.

Usage

correctSFSBias(sfs, method = c("truncation", "binomial"))

Arguments

sfs

A WithinHostSFS object.

method

Character. Correction method: "truncation" (default) rescales the whole spectrum for the unobservable part of the frequency range; "binomial" models the probability of detecting a variant at each frequency given the read depth.

Value

A corrected WithinHostSFS with corrected = TRUE. Counts are no longer raw variant counts, and nSites changes accordingly, which also changes the number of segregating sites used by neutralityFromSFS. Use uncorrected spectra for compareSFS.

Details

This function applies a correction based on the expected number of unobserved sites under a neutral beta distribution model: given the observed SFS and depth-dependent detectability, it estimates the missing mass in the lowest frequency bins.

The "truncation" method assumes a uniform density of variant frequencies and multiplies every bin by \(f_{max} / (f_{max} - \mathrm{threshold})\), the reciprocal of the observable fraction of the frequency range. It therefore rescales the spectrum without changing its shape. The "binomial" method uses the stored depth to compute \(P(\mathrm{detect} | \nu, n) = P(\mathrm{Alt} \ge k_{\min} | n, \nu)\) where \(k_{\min} = \lceil n \times \mathrm{threshold} \rceil\), and reweights each bin by the inverse of its detectability. Detectability is floored at 0.01, so a bin is inflated at most one hundredfold.

Either way the corrected counts stay whole numbers of sites, as fusFs needs a whole number of segregating sites. The corrected total is rounded once, and its sites are shared out among the bins by largest remainder, ties going to the lower bins; rounding each bin on its own would leave every bin of a few sites unchanged. nSites is that total.

Examples

vcf <- system.file("extdata", "test_donor.vcf",
    package = "WithinHostExperiment")
whe <- readWithinHost(vcf,
    colData = S4Vectors::DataFrame(sample_id = "donor"),
    caller = "ivar")
sfs <- buildSFS(whe, genomeLength = 1000L)
sfs_corr <- correctSFSBias(sfs, method = "binomial")
sfs_corr
#> WithinHostSFS with 15 variants in 20 bins
#>   sample: donor 
#>   folded: TRUE 
#>   polarization: none 
#>   threshold: 0.03 
#>   corrected: TRUE 
#>   genome: 1000 bp
#>   median depth: 1600 x
